Grain size analysis test on RSM-b soil (Mixture of RS and Crushed Marbel (MS) (narrowly graded)), dense; apparatus: sieve analysis (U.S. Std. Sieve No. axis of the chart). Recorded: percent finer vs grain size (average and range).

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
The numbers below were digitized from the published figure by two readings made separately; they agree within the stated reading bounds at 136 of the 185 points, and 35 are still under review. They have not yet been checked by a person. The test setup is incomplete: relative density Dr, tool, bin or mold, fill depth, control, rate are not reported.
:::

## Data

![percent finer than by weight against grain size, SI units. Error bars are reading bounds (half-widths from the digitization), not standard deviations. Filled markers were agreed by both readings, hollow ones were not.](../img/plots/b68-gs-fa-46.png){.lightbox}

Peak percent finer than by weight 101 percent at 4.48 mm grain size; 101 percent at 4.58 mm, the end of the record.

Download: [observations.csv](../files/data/experiments/b68-gs-fa-46/observations.csv) (185 points: 20 plotted symbols, 153 samples of the drawn curve; columns `x_si`, `y_si` with bounds `x_bound_si`, `y_bound_si`; panel 1: percent finer than by weight (a fraction of 1) against grain size in m; the printed-unit values, the pixel position on the scan and the review status of each point are kept in further columns) and [series.json](../files/data/experiments/b68-gs-fa-46/series.json) (units, conversion factors, how the points were read).

Reading bounds on this figure (how far our reading of the printed figure may be off, not the uncertainty of the test): typical bound 27 micrometers in grain size, 1.05 percentage points in percent finer than by weight (1.0 percent of the peak). Both independent readings agree within these bounds at 136 of the 185 points; 35 are still under review (hollow in the plot) and 14 were settled against the scan. [Check the digitized points against the scan](../figures/index.qmd#check-fa-46).
